findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when file is missing, unreadable, or not valid UTF-8
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the process instead of returning a typed error that the shell can handle gracefully
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))?, and remove unwrap()

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked indexing into a Vec<String> with no bounds validation after split
findings.failure_mode: a malformed line with fewer than expected fields panics at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use parts.get(0).ok_or(ParseError::MissingField("name")) and guard the split result length before indexing

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() combines unchecked indexing and a second unwrap on parse, both panicking on malformed input
findings.failure_mode: a line missing a second field or containing a non-numeric value causes a panic rather than returning a typed parse or allocation error
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::MissingField("value"))?.trim().parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue) and return typed errors through map_err

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy as conversion that silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: sensor values in the range 65536-4294967295 wrap to incorrect smaller values with no error, corrupting data silently
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::OutOfRange) after successful parse to ensure values fit and failures are typed

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds hidden I/O (stdout logging) inside the data-parsing closure that should be pure calculation
findings.failure_mode: side-effectful logging leaks into the calculation layer, making the function non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and violating Data/Calculations/Actions separation
findings.fix: remove println! from the parser closure; return a pure parsed Record and let the shell layer handle all logging and I/O separately

findings.problem: Record.name is a raw String with no domain invariants; any code path can assign an empty, null-containing, or otherwise invalid string
findings.failure_mode: downstream logic consuming Record cannot assume name is a valid sensor identifier, breaking invariants and making illegal states representable
findings.fix: introduce a newtype SensorName(String) with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and valid characters, and use SensorName in Record

findings.problem: no benchmark exists for load_sensors to validate allocation behavior or performance characteristics of the unbounded Vec<String> collect
findings.failure_mode: without benchmark or profiler evidence, the allocation pattern (per-line String allocation, Vec::with_capacity guess, intermediate allocations) cannot be verified as acceptable for the workload
findings.fix: add a criterion or similar benchmark measuring memory allocations and throughput against representative sensor CSV data, and report workload/hardware details

findings.problem: no input length cap, no try_reserve, and no max_items validation before collecting parsed lines into Vec; unbounded allocation from external file input
findings.failure_mode: a large or malicious CSV file causes unbounded memory allocation, potentially exhausting memory without graceful error recovery
findings.fix: add a max_items domain cap, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? after cap validation, and enforce the cap before each push

findings.problem: no CLI binary, command script, or test harness exists to exercise load_sensors end-to-end with real file paths and hostile inputs
findings.failure_mode: without command-truth evidence, the parsing, error handling, and domain construction cannot be verified against real-world hostile inputs
findings.fix: add a bin target or integration test that exercises load_sensors with valid CSV, missing-file, malformed-fields, and oversized-input cases

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sensors allocation and throughput
no profiler evidence for memory traffic and hot-path behavior
no allocation analysis (no try_reserve, no input cap, no max_items)
no command evidence (no binary or integration test exercising load_sensors end-to-end)
residual_risk: Static review identified 6 BLOCKER violations (2 unwrap panics, 2 unchecked index accesses, 1 lossy cast, 1 hidden I/O, 1 raw-string domain primitive) and 3 WARNING/INFO gaps. No commands were executed. The function fuses file I/O, parsing, validation, and stdout logging in a single untyped path with no error taxonomy, no input caps, and no allocation bounds. A full repair would require: introducing Result return with typed errors (Io, MissingField, InvalidValue, OutOfRange, Allocation), removing all unwrap and unchecked indexing, removing println! from the closure, adding max_items cap with try_reserve, introducing SensorName newtype, and adding benchmark/integration tests.
